greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. May the peace of the Lord be with you all.
penitential:
Lord, have mercy.
Christ, have mercy.
Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: I love you, Lord, my strength.
homily:
We often think of the law as a set of fences. We imagine life as a large field, and the commandments as the wire, keeping us from wandering into the weeds or the cliff’s edge. But when the scholar of the law asks Jesus which commandment is the greatest, he is not asking for a fence. He is asking for a center. He is asking: 'What is the heartbeat of all of this?'

Jesus answers with a movement of the heart that is total. 'You shall love the Lord, your God, with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.' It is a beautiful, terrifying, and all-consuming invitation. It is not a request for a portion of our time or a sliver of our concern. It is a call to be entirely, completely, and joyfully given over to the One who created us.

Think for a moment of a compass. When a needle is perfectly balanced, it doesn't hesitate; it points true north. That is what Jesus is describing for the human soul. When our heart, our soul, and our mind are all aligned in the same direction—toward God—we find a kind of freedom that nothing in this world can touch. We see this in the First Reading today, where God reminds his people to care for the vulnerable, the widow, and the orphan. Why? Because the love of God is not a private feeling; it is a public, concrete, living reality. If you love the Source of Life, you cannot help but love the lives He has created.

I think of Benjamin Vo. I think of how he navigated the world with that same sort of alignment. You remember how he was—this brilliant, curious mind, always diving into the logic of mathematics, the systems of AI, the complex architecture of cloud infrastructure. But his mind was never just for himself. It was a mind that loved. He was the boy who sat with his father, mapping out the future, dreaming of 'con chim airlines' with a giggle that could light up a room. He was the boy who, in the quiet sincerity of his heart, offered everything he had—his entire piggy bank—to help his uncle in a time of need. He didn't need to empty it, and he didn't need to break it. The beauty wasn't in the transaction; it was in the offer. It was the sign of a heart that was already, in its own young way, pointing toward the greatest commandment.

There is a profound truth here for all of us, especially when the weight of life feels heavy. We often wonder if we are doing enough, or if we are being 'good' enough. We look at our own lives and see the gaps. We see the things we left unsaid, the moments we were distracted, the days we felt we failed the people we love. We carry a silent, nagging guilt, wondering if we missed a sign or could have done more. But look at the Gospel again. Jesus does not ask for perfection. He asks for love. He asks for the heart. He asks for the soul. He asks for the mind. When we offer those to Him, He takes whatever we have—even if it feels like a small, unopened piggy bank—and He makes it a gift.

Alan, Thao, and Ryan, I know that the silence in your home can sometimes feel like a physical weight. I know that there are mornings when the sun hits the floorboards and you are hit, all over again, by the reality of the empty space where Ben should be. You are not alone in that ache. But remember that love is not lost. The love you have for Benjamin, and the love he had for you, is not a thing that died with his body. It is a part of that 'greatest commandment.' It is a part of the eternal life that Jesus promises. Because Ben loved you with all his heart, and because you loved him with all yours, you are bound together in the very life of God. That bond is not broken by death; it is only hidden from our sight for a little while.

There is a story about a gondola ride in Venice—a moment of laughter, a family gathered together, braces flashing in a bright, sunny selfie. That is not just a memory. That is a witness. It is a witness to the fact that you lived, you loved, and you were a family. God does not forget those moments. He holds them in the palm of His hand. When you feel that grief ambushing you, when you feel the urge to blame yourselves or to wonder why things happened as they did, I want you to hear the voice of the Lord: 'I am compassionate.' He does not accuse you. He does not hold your sorrow against you. He stands with you in the middle of it, just as you stood with Ben in his own moments of struggle. You were his comfort then; God is your comfort now.

What does it mean to live for Ben today? It means to live with the same curiosity and the same kindness he showed. It means to look at the world—at the birds, at the airplanes, at the people in need—and to see them through the eyes of love. It means to be the 'funny dad' who tells stories, and to be the brother who carries a piece of his sibling’s joy into the future. Ryan, you are a gift to your parents, and you were the best friend Ben could have asked for. Keep dreaming, keep building, keep laughing. Every time you look at the sky and see a jet climbing into the clouds, know that the love you shared is still soaring.

We are all, in a sense, like those who were once aliens in a strange land. We are all waiting to go home. And while we are here, our task is simple: to love the Lord, and to love our neighbor as ourselves. It is a small, doable thing. It is a matter of being kind to the person in front of you. It is a matter of saying 'good morning' with the same consistency Ben did. It is a matter of offering what you have, even if you keep it tucked away in your heart, as a sign of your willingness to give.

Today, take this with you: You are held. You are not forgotten. The God who hears the cry of the widow and the orphan is the same God who holds Benjamin in the light of His presence. And because He is the God of the living, you are never truly separated from the one you love. When you go out that door, try to see one person today with the gentle, curious eyes that Ben had. Offer one small act of kindness in his name. And when the day ends, as you lay your head down, remember that you are loved by the Father, by the Son, and by the Holy Spirit, now and forever. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may His face shine upon you always. Go in peace.
standing_petitions: Benjamin Vo ammalu kikkut tamaita quviasunniqarniqpata Ataniup qaningani, nalligijavut aniguqtilaaqtut.
Kikkut tamaita uqumaittumik atuqtut, Ataniup asannininga qaninganiittuq, nalligijavut aniguqtilaaqtut.

readings.label: Atuagait 1
readings.text: Ataniq uqaqtuq: 'Inuit iksivautami inuusiq, iksivautami inuit. Iksivautami inuit, kikkut nalligijavut aniguqtilaaqtut. Iksivautami inuit, kikkut nalligijavut aniguqtilaaqtut. Iksivautami inuit, kikkut nalligijavut aniguqtilaaqtut.'

readings.label: Tusaajautit
readings.text: R. Asagivagit, Ataniq, sannginirpaaq. Asagivagit, O Ataniq, sannginirpaaq, O Ataniq, qaarjuq, qamut, aniguqtirijuq. R. Asagivagit, Ataniq, sannginirpaaq. Ataniq inuujuq ammalu quviasukli qaarjuq! Atuagait Ataniq aniguqtirijuq.

readings.label: Atuagait 2
readings.text: Qatanngutit: Qaujimajusi qanuq inuusiqarpugut ilissinni. Ilissik ajjiuqattatut ilitturijauniqtuq, nalligijavut aniguqtilaaqtut. Ilissik ataniup uqausinga tusaajariaqarpugut, ammalu ataniup asannininga ilisimallugu.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text: Jesus uqaqtuq: 'Asagivagit Ataniq, Godit, tamainnik inuusiup iluani. Taanna anginiqpaaq ammalu sivulliqpaaq. Aippaa ajjiuqattatut: Asagivagit qanigijavut ajjiuqattatut.' Taanna tamainnik inuusiup iluani.

pet_prayers.text: Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.
